Struggling with my sexuality my whole life has always been something that I ignored. I didn’t want to be gay or bisexual so I ignored it. I thought if I pretended it wasn’t real, then that meant that it really wasn’t. And even now I struggle even saying it out loud.
I grew up with a mother who never spoke about LGBT+ topics and a father who, when he did talk about it, was making fun of it or questioning it. And two older sisters who spoke of it rarely.

And when I find myself liking a girl I think it’s weird and I have to remind myself that it’s normal and it’s okay. And especially with my gender, which changes often because I’m still confused. Female just doesn’t feel like me, but nb or male don’t feel right either?

Then, at my gsa club, I heard it. Bisexual. All of a sudden it made sense. But that didn’t mean it was okay. Just because I had an explanation doesn’t mean I wasn’t wrong. Or broken. I hated myself for a really long time.

Not only was my sexuality wrong, so was my gender. The self hatred only got worse. And by the time I even got close to accepting my non-binaryness even just a little I started thinking no one would accept me because I didn’t dress or look androgynous. I looked like a girl.

This obviously did nothing. I started allowing myself to be around toxic friends. I was letting these transphobic people into my life and I never complained. To have friends that I can never come out to because they’d reject me, but they’re my only friends, is toxic.

At this point my self image was shattered. I absolutely hated myself. And I resented the universe for making me this way. And even though I’m an atheist, and even though I resent religion, i went to synagogue and I prayed. I begged God, if he’s even real, to just make me normal.

I had no one to come out to. No friends, no parents, only my sister Hannah. Everyone else would judge me and reject me. That’s why pride parades are so important. And that’s why having LGBT friends here on Twitter is so important.
